title: How Does GPS Know Exactly Where You Are? 🛰️
description: Your phone never sends anything to GPS satellites — it just listens to time signals and does some clever math. And without Einstein's relativity, GPS would drift by kilometers every single day!

scenes.say: You open your map, and within seconds your phone knows where you are, down to a few meters. So how does GPS actually work?

scenes.label: About 31 satellites
scenes.say: About thirty-one satellites orbit twenty thousand kilometers above us, and each one constantly broadcasts the exact time and its own position.

scenes.caption: Your phone only listens
scenes.say: Your phone never sends anything to the satellites. It only receives their signals and measures how long each one took to arrive.
From the travel time, it works out the distance to each satellite. With at least four satellites, those distances cross at a single point. That point is you.

scenes.text: Satellite clocks gain 38 microseconds a day
scenes.say: Here's the twist: thanks to Einstein's relativity, satellite clocks run thirty-eight microseconds fast every day. Without correcting that, GPS would be off by about ten kilometers a day!
